native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Prevalence of non-native plants introduced through the Gardening pathway varies strongly with habitat type: it is highest in human-used lowland habitats — Wetlands (n.gard>0 in 50.0% of 38 plots, mean n.gard 0.76, n.gard/n.total = 29/52 = 0.56), Urban (47.7% of 65 plots, 0.69, 45/151 = 0.30), Coastal (44.8% of 29 plots, 0.79, 23/43 = 0.53) and Riparian (36.1% of 61 plots, 0.57, 35/96 = 0.36), which hold 78% of all 169 n.gard records on only 31% of the 632 plots — and it is much lower in Croplands (20.7% of plots, mean n.gard 0.22, share 20/108 = 0.19, where 83 of 108 records are Unintentional) and in Meadows (7.7%). Habitat types with almost no invasion records (Coniferous and Broad-leaved forests, Scrublands, Rock outcrops; 18 records over 308 plots) are gardening-rare per plot (occupancy 0-6.5%), so their high formal shares (0.875, 1.000) are small-sample artefacts and do not mean forests are dominated by garden plants.
